items.content: Process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy. Plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to produce oxygen and glucose.
Force that attracts objects with mass. Everything in the universe experiences gravity. It keeps planets in orbit and objects on the ground.
Continuous process where water evaporates from surfaces, condenses in the atmosphere, and falls as precipitation. Essential for life on Earth.
Process in cells that breaks down glucose to release energy. Occurs in mitochondria. Opposite of photosynthesis in many ways.
Double helix molecule containing genetic instructions. Made of adenine, thymine, guanine, and cytosine bases. Carries hereditary information.
Study of heat, energy, and work. First law: energy cannot be created or destroyed. Second law: entropy increases in isolated systems.
